=== CONCLUSION ===
This paper describes a 3D-printed microfluidic device for culturing patient-derived
tumor spheroids and performing drug screening. It reports qualitative correlations
(color-coded heat maps, trends) between ex vivo spheroid viability/area changes and
clinical outcomes for 10 patients. However, NO global quantitative clinical/toxicity
headline metric (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, AUC, correlation coefficient, etc.)
is reported. The paper explicitly notes it is a small-scale proof-of-concept study.
Therefore: status = no_headline.

unit.explanation: Ten patients (T1-T10) with tumor-derived spheroids tested ex vivo

platform.explanation: Patient-derived multicellular spheroids cultured in 3D-printed microfluidic device

readout.explanation: WST-1 viability assay and spheroid area change measured 7 days post-treatment

direction.explanation: Reduction in viability indicates drug sensitivity

threshold_rule.explanation: Color-coded qualitative trend map (green/red/white) but no binary classification threshold defined

threshold_timing.explanation: No binary threshold was applied; qualitative comparison only

patient_mapping.explanation: Individual patients T1-T10 identified in Table 1 and Fig 5 data

regimen_match.explanation: Ex vivo drug concentrations set by IC50, not matched to patient clinical doses; qualitative trend comparison

split.explanation: Same 10 patients used for both ex vivo testing and clinical comparison; no train/test split

headline.blocked_reason: No global quantitative clinical/toxicity headline metric (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, AUC, or correlation coefficient) is reported. The paper presents only qualitative color-coded trend comparisons (green/red/white heat map) between ex vivo spheroid viability/area changes and clinical outcomes for 10 patients, explicitly described as a small-scale proof-of-concept study without a summary statistic.

notes: The paper reports qualitative correlations: T1, T6, T10 show direct trend between viability reduction and clinical responsiveness (article:p30).
Fig 5d heat map uses green/red/white color coding but no numeric summary metric is provided.
The supplementary data (Fig. 5 sheet) contains per-patient viability reduction values but no binary clinical outcome labels suitable for computing accuracy/sensitivity/specificity.
Table 1 provides clinical treatment responses in text form (partial remission, stable disease, deterioration) but these are not converted to a quantitative headline.
